land.text: Herat and its district: the Karts 'began as subordinates of the Ghurid sultan, then became vassal princes within the Mongol Empire'

predecessors.note: The infobox names the Ilkhanate as predecessor; in 1244 the overlord was the Mongol Empire.

land.text: Herat and the Kart lands of Khorasan, taken by Timur in 1381

capitals.name: Herat
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Herat'. Khaysar appears on the page only as the place where Rukn-uddin died (3 September 1305).

correction.text: Herat and a large part of Khorasan, as a vassal principality of the Mongols; the 1344 outline is the nearest available shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1244-1343 for the years before Cliopatria's row. The page gives 'Foundation by Malik Rukn-uddin Abu Bakr: 1244' (text: Shams-uddin Muhammad 'founded the dynasty in 1245') and 'a large part of Khorasan', ruled first as 'vassal princes within the Mongol Empire'; no towns or boundaries are dated before 1342, so the 1344 outline is the nearest shape. Unverified: page budget.

474,469 km2 for 1344-1351: Herat, Ghor, Badghis, Farah, part of Khorasan and Turkmenistan. The page names only 'a large part of Khorasan' and 'Afghanistan, Iran, and Turkmenistan' as today's territory, which the shape matches; no list of towns or area. After the Ilkhanate's fragmentation (1335) Husayn 'worked to expand his principality'; in 1349 he stopped paying tribute to Togha Temur and 'ruled as an independent Sultan'. Unverified: page budget.
474,716 km2 for 1352-1374: the 1344 shape with a trivial change. Around 1358 Qazaghan 'invaded Khurasan and sacked Herat' (a raid, not a change of owner). Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the 1375 shape plus Nishapur and its district, valid 1375-1381

keyframe_review.note: 576,490 km2 for 1375-1384: the shape grows by about 100,000 km2 into South and Razavi Khorasan, but checked on the gazetteer it does not contain Nishapur, which the Sarbadars page gives to the Kartids of Pir 'Ali after Sabzavar (c. 1376): 'At about the same time, Nishapur was conquered by the Kartids of Pir 'Ali'; the Kart page says around 1375 or 1376. Cliopatria's Sarbadars shape still holds Nishapur in 1380. The shape also runs three years past the end: Herat fell in April 1381 and Cliopatria's 1384 is the later execution of Pir Ali's family.

ledger.note: 1244: Malik Rukn-uddin Abu Bakr founds the Kart dynasty at Herat. Infobox 'Foundation by Malik Rukn-uddin Abu Bakr: 1244'; the text says Shams-uddin Muhammad 'founded the dynasty in 1245'. The Karts are 'vassal princes within the Mongol Empire'; the Mongol dossiers should carry the vassalage.
About 1376: Pir 'Ali's Karts take Nishapur. The page: Pir Ali 'took Nishapur around 1375 or 1376'; the Sarbadars page has it conquered 'at about the same time' as Sabzavar (c. 1376).

region.text: Herat and the Kart lands of Khorasan

ledger.note: 1381: Timur takes Herat and ends the Kart state. 'In April 1381, Timur arrived before the city.' Herat then fell and Ghiyas-uddin Pir 'Ali and his son 'were carried off to Samarkand'.

region.text: Herat and the Kart lands of Khorasan

ledger.note: 1381: the Kart dynasty ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1381'; Pir Ali's rebellion of 1382 and his execution around 1383 followed, and the page adds that 'The remaining Karts were murdered in 1396 at a banquet by Miran Shah'. Cliopatria keeps the row to 1384.

wars.name: Battle of Zava
wars.outcome: The Karts won on 18 July 1342 after disunity in the Sarbadar army; no frontier changed.
wars.note: The Sarbadars page dates the same clash to 1342 without a full date.

wars.name: Sarbadar-Kartid conflict
wars.outcome: Fighting continued after Husayn's death in 1370; Pir Ali's Karts took Nishapur around 1376.
wars.note: The Sarbadars page states the Kartids 'still was a danger' in 1349 and that fighting with the Sarbadars continued after 1370.

wars.name: Qazaghan's invasion of Khurasan
wars.outcome: The Chagatai amir Qazaghan 'invaded Khurasan and sacked Herat' around 1358; Qazaghan was later assassinated.
wars.note: Cliopatria's Chagatai Khanate row is a neighbour only to 1351.

wars.name: Timur's conquest of Herat
wars.outcome: Timur arrived before Herat in April 1381; the city fell and Pir Ali and his son were taken to Samarkand.
wars.note: Pir Ali supported a rebellion in 1382 and was executed around 1383.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line; the Sarbadar frontier around Nishapur and Sabzavar and the Turkmen steppe edge are approximate.

sources.title: Kart dynasty
sources.note: Identity, infobox 1244-1381, Husayn 1332-1370, Zava 1342, Qazaghan c. 1358, Timur 1381.

sources.title: Sarbadars
sources.note: Counterpart: Nishapur taken by the Kartids c. 1376, Sarbadar-Kart fighting, Cliopatria's Sarbadars shape holds Nishapur in 1380.

notes: Pages: two (budget 1-2). Start 1244 is the infobox's (the text says 1245); Cliopatria's row begins in 1344, when the Karts were already 'vassal princes' of the Mongols and then of the Ilkhanate: the Mongol Empire and Ilkhanate dossiers should carry the vassalage (1244-1349) and the Kart state is drawn here as a vassal principality on the 1344 outline, which is unverified for 1244-1343. Independence: 'Husayn stopped paying tribute to Togha Temur in 1349 and ruled as an independent Sultan' has no ledger type of its own and is in the keyframe note. End 1381 (infobox) against Cliopatria's 1384; the page's reign table gives Pir Ali 1370-1389 and a 1383 execution, and says the remaining Karts were murdered in 1396, so the dynasty's final date is conflicted. No ruler list was extracted (only Husayn 1332-1370, Pir Ali from 1370 and Rukn-uddin d. 3 September 1305), so identity.rulers is omitted. Not settled: the page does not mention Husayn's conquests of Ghor, Badghis, Sistan, Farah, Marw, Tus or Sarakhs, so those parts of the 1344 shape are unverified; the Sarbadars page has Malik Muhammad using Sarakhs as a base after 1370 while Pir Ali 'inherited most of the Kart lands'. Cliopatria's Sarbadars shape holds Nishapur in 1380, contradicting the Kartid gain c. 1376.
